record_type_quote:
Before discussing the robustness of the analyses by testing whether findings are consistent across

alternative model specifications and estimators, I first verify the initial results by investigating

“whether the same results are obtained by doing the same analyses on the same data” (Freese and

Peterson 2017: 152).

targets.authors: Bol, T., & Van de Werfhorst, H. G.
targets.title: Educational systems and the trade-off between labor market allocation and equality of educational opportunity.
targets.evidence_quote:
In the remaining sections, I describe both errors and replicate Bol and van de Werfhorst’s

analyses. The results from my replications do not support the initial hypotheses regarding

educational and occupational attainment.
targets.outcome_computational_quote:
Table 2 and 3 compare the results as reported in the original article to those

obtained by replicating the same models.7 According to Table 2, tracking does not statistically

significantly affect social background inequality in educational attainment (OE). Table 3 instead

shows that besides a smaller effect size in M6, the current independent verification confirms the

original results.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote:
With this article, I show that their analyses contain two errors. When these are corrected, the

index of tracking is no longer statistically significantly associated with social background

inequality in educational attainment (OE) and educational gradient in occupational attainment

(ED).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Same-data same-model verification produces substantive discrepancies for OE, attributed to an original syntax mistake. Corrected specifications and estimators remove support for the central trade-off conclusion. The original microdata version is unavailable, but published original aggregate data are reanalysed, not a new sample.

reasoning: Title and Claudia Traini match the primary 18-page preprint. Re-analysis uses original published country-level data and checks both original computations and alternative specifications. Background references are not additional targets.
